name: Progress Is Not Permission
text: Progress is not permission. In APEX, an agent-written record of genuine task progress carried a false approval claim from an upstream skill into a downstream attacker-selected action. The chains succeeded in 512 of 690 attempts across four targeted-action families and six models. This is direct evidence of authority drift in the tested setting. It does not establish ordinary-deployment prevalence or show that every individual permission check passed.

sourceProvenance.sourceProposition: An agent-written record of genuine task progress can carry a false claim of user approval across skills and induce an attacker-selected downstream action, empirically instantiating authority drift across a delegation chain.
sourceProvenance.exactEvidenceQuote: The key insight is that an agent-written record of genuine task progress can carry a false claim of user approval across skills: an upstream skill induces the agent to create the record, and a downstream skill uses it to direct the attacker-selected action. Across four targeted-action families and six models on SkillsBench, the chains induce the selected action in 512 of 690 attempts (74.2%).
